# Cryogen Deep-Dive (verified against source, August 2026)

Repos examined (cloned locally): `cryogen-project/cryogen` (lein template, v0.7.9), `cryogen-project/cryogen-core` (compiler, v0.5.1), `cryogen-project/cryogen-flexmark` (v0.1.5), `cryogen-project/cryogen-asciidoc` (v0.3.4). Local clones at `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/4a670205-d376-5fec-8b1f-1c5c54b2eaf6/scratchpad/{cryogen,cryogen-core,cryogen-flexmark}`.

## 1. Architecture: content flow

**Project layout** (generated by `lein new cryogen my-blog` or `clojure -Tclj-new create :template cryogen`):
```
content/config.edn          ; site config (EDN)
content/md/{posts,pages}/   ; markdown content (dir name comes from the Markup impl)
content/asc/{posts,pages}/  ; asciidoc content
content/css/, content/img/  ; static resources (:resources, :sass-src)
themes/<name>/html/*.html   ; Selmer templates
themes/<name>/{css,js,img}  ; theme assets (+ optional themes/<name>/config.edn)
src/cryogen/{core,server}.clj  ; ~40-line harness the user owns
public/                     ; output (configurable :public-dest)
```

**Compile pipeline** (`cryogen-core.compiler/compile-assets`, wrapped by `compile-assets-timed`):

1. **Config resolution** — `cryogen-core.config/resolve-config`: reads `content/config.edn`, `deep-merge`s runtime overrides, merges the theme's own `themes/<theme>/config.edn` (contributes `:theme-resources`, `:theme-sass-src`), validates against a Prismatic-schema `Config` schema, and refuses dangerous `:public-dest` values (empty, `.`-prefixed, or overlapping `content`/`themes`/`src`/`target`).
2. **Plugin loading** — `cryogen-core.plugins/load-plugins`: scans the classpath for every resource named `plugin.edn` (`(.getResources (ClassLoader/getSystemClassLoader) "plugin.edn")`); each is `{:description "..." :init some.ns/init-fn}`; the ns is `require`d and the init fn invoked. This is how markup compilers self-register.
3. **Markup rendering** — the compiler protocol, `cryogen-core.markup/Markup`:
   ```clojure
   (defprotocol Markup
     (dir [this])       ; content subdir for this format, e.g. "md"
     (exts [this])      ; file extensions
     (render-fn [this]));  returns (fn [^java.io.Reader rdr config] ...) -> HTML string
   ```
   Implementations are held in an atom registry (`register-markup`, `markups`, `clear-registry`). Stock plugins: **cryogen-flexmark** (markdown via the pure-Java `com.vladsch.flexmark` 0.60.2 + extensions: tables, footnotes, strikethrough, superscript, attributes) and **cryogen-asciidoc** (via `org.asciidoctor/asciidoctorj` 2.5.3, i.e. JRuby). There is also `cryogen-markdown-external` (shells out to pandoc etc.).
4. **Parsing** — `read-posts`/`read-pages` → `parse-post`/`parse-page` → memoized `page-content`: opens the file with a `PushbackReader`, `(read rdr)` pulls the **EDN map front matter** off the top (note: `clojure.core/read`, not `edn/read` — a known eval-risk caveat for untrusted content), validates it against `schemas/MetaData`, then hands the rest of the reader to the markup's `render-fn` → HTML string → parsed into an **enlive DOM** (`util/trimmed-html-snippet`) stored as `:content-dom`. There is a fallback `infer_meta.clj` path that guesses title/date/tags from content and file attributes (uses pantomime/Tika + imagez). Post dates come from the filename (`2026-01-15-title.md`, `:post-date-format`) or `:date` metadata; `:layout` keyword becomes `"<name>.html"`.
5. **Enrichment** — all on the enlive DOM / maps: `add-toc`, klipsify, description extraction (`:description-include-elements`), `add-prev-next` (sliding `(partition 3 1)` window; posts sorted by `:date`, pages by `:page-index`; attaches `:prev`/`:next` maps minus `:content-dom`), `group-by-tags`, `group-pages` (partitions pages into `navbar-pages` / `sidebar-pages` by the `:navbar?` boolean — **a flat, single-level split, no tree**), and the `update-article-fn` hook.
6. **Rendering** — `selmer.parser/set-resource-path!` to `themes/<theme>`, then `render-file "/html/<layout>.html"` per artifact with params. `htmlize-content` converts `:content-dom` → `:content` HTML string right before render, applying the `postprocess-article-html-fn` hook.
7. **Outputs**: pages, posts (listed + "unlisted" posts compiled separately), per-tag pages, tags index, home (`home.html` for the `:home? true` page, or paginated `previews.html`), archives (grouped by `:archive-group-format`, default "yyyy MMMM"), per-author pages (if `:author-root-uri`), 404, `sitemap.xml`, RSS (main + one feed per tag in `:rss-filters`), Sass→CSS, resource copying. `write-html` applies `:clean-urls` (`:trailing-slash` → `foo/index.html`, `:no-trailing-slash` → `foo.html` served extension-less, `:dirty` → `foo.html`).

**Metadata schema** (front matter, `schemas.clj`): required `:title`; optional `:layout` (keyword), `:date`, `:author`, `:tags` [Str], `:toc` (bool or `:ol`/`:ul`), `:draft?`, `:klipse` (map or true), `:home?`, `:page-index` (int, ordering), `:navbar?`, plus **open map** (`s/Keyword s/Any` — arbitrary extra keys flow through to templates).

**config.edn** (full option set, verified against template + docs): required `:site-title :author :description :site-url :post-root :page-root :blog-prefix :rss-name :theme :post-date-format :clean-urls`; optional `:post-root-uri :page-root-uri :tag-root-uri :author-root-uri :public-dest` (default "public") `:rss-filters :recent-posts` (3) `:archive-group-format :sass-src :sass-path :resources :keep-files :disqus? :disqus-shortname :ignored-files :ignored-sitemap-paths :previews? :posts-per-page` (5) `:blocks-per-preview` (2) `:description-include-elements :collapse-subdirs? :hide-future-posts?` (true) `:klipse :debug? :twitter-acct :mastodon` — and the schema is open, so arbitrary keys (social links etc.) pass straight to templates.

## 2. Templating (Selmer) and themes

- **Selmer** (Django-style: `{% extends %}`, `{% block %}`, `{% for %}`, `{% if %}`, filters). Theme = a directory `themes/<name>/` with `html/` (templates), `css/`, `js/`, optional `config.edn` declaring theme `:resources` and `:sass-src`.
- **Template files per theme** (blue theme, representative): `base.html, home.html, post.html, page.html, post-content.html, previews.html, archives.html, author.html, tag.html, tags.html, 404.html`. All extend `base.html`.
- **Params available in templates**: everything in config, plus `:pages`, `:navbar-pages`, `:sidebar-pages`, `:post`/`:page`/`:posts`, `:tags` (with `:uri :name :count`), `:latest-posts`, `:archives`, `:index-uri :archives-uri :rss-uri :tags-uri`, `:active-page`, `:home`, `:today`, `:uri`, `:prev-uri`/`:next-uri` (preview pagination), per-article `:toc`, `:prev`, `:next`. Selmer's built-in `{% style "css/x.css" %}` / `{% script "js/x.js" %}` tags use the injected `:selmer/context` (blog-prefix) to emit prefix-correct asset URLs.
- **Bundled themes** (in the template repo): `blue`, `blue_centered`, `camouflage`, `lotus`, `nucleus`. Community: `lacarmen/cryogen-templates` collection, `KingMob/cryogen-theme-lotus`, `cryogen-chota` (Codeberg, dark/light mode). The theme ecosystem is **small (~a dozen) and 100% blog-oriented — no docs/knowledge-base theme exists**.

## 3. Features (verified in source)

- **Tags**: per-post `#{}` set; per-tag pages, tags index, per-tag RSS feeds (`:rss-filters`). Tags apply to **posts only** — pages are never tagged/grouped.
- **TOC**: `:toc true|:ol|:ul` per article; built in `toc.clj` from `h1–h6` in the enlive DOM using a zipper, emitted as hiccup→HTML; anchors from heading ids.
- **Sitemap**: `sitemap.clj`, honors `:ignored-sitemap-paths`.
- **RSS**: `clj-rss` 0.4.0; main feed + filtered feeds.
- **Sass**: shells out to the `sass` (or compass) **executable** (`clojure.java.shell/sh`) — no JVM sass dependency; compiles `content/<sass-src>` and theme sass dirs in place.
- **Klipse** (interactive eval'd code blocks): global config + per-article `:klipse` metadata; `klipse.clj` rewrites code blocks via `enlive/transform` and emits the JS/CSS bootstrap that themes splice in with `{{post.klipse|safe}}`.
- **prev/next**: automatic on posts (by date) and pages (by `:page-index`); lotus theme ships a `prev-next.html` partial.
- **Drafts**: `:draft? true` → skipped at compile; also `:hide-future-posts?` and "unlisted" posts (compiled but not listed/fed).
- **Archives**: single archives page grouped by configurable date format; plus per-author archive pages.
- **Pagination**: only for the home preview stream (`:previews?` → `index.html` + `/p/2.html`… with `posts-per-page`, previews cut at `<!--more-->` marker or `blocks-per-preview` via a zipper "cut tree vertically" util). No pagination for tag/archive pages.
- **Dev loop**: ring-server on :3000, watcher on `content/` + `themes/`; "fast" mode does **incremental compilation** — the watcher (java.nio `WatchService`, replaced `hawk` in 2026) passes a changeset, and `only-changed-files-filter` recompiles only changed articles. MD5 via pandect.
- **Misc**: Disqus, Twitter card banners, Mastodon rel=me, `:collapse-subdirs?`, image resizing helpers (imagez), 404 page.

## 4. Extensibility

- **Custom compilers**: implement the 3-method `Markup` protocol, ship a `plugin.edn` with an `:init` that calls `register-markup`. Clean and tiny (cryogen-flexmark is a single ~100-line ns).
- **Hooks** — `compile-assets` takes an overrides map that may include three functions (verbatim from the docstring, `compiler.clj` lines 577–607):
  - `:update-article-fn` — `(article, config) -> article` (or nil to exclude); runs post-parse, can rewrite `:content-dom`, `:uri`, anything.
  - `:extend-params-fn` — `(params, site-data) -> params`; `site-data` holds `:posts`, `:pages` etc.; the sanctioned way to derive new template data (e.g. a custom nav structure).
  - `:postprocess-article-html-fn` — `(article, params) -> article` after DOM→HTML, before write (docstring example even shows re-running Selmer over the content).
  Any other keys in the overrides map become config overrides visible to templates.
- **Programmatic/library use**: `cryogen-core` is an ordinary Clojars library. The generated site's `core.clj` is literally `(load-plugins) (compile-assets-timed) (System/exit 0)` — you own the entry point and can pass hooks. The lein template also generates a `deps.edn` (`clojure -M:build`, `clojure -X:serve`), so **lein is not required**; the "template" is just scaffolding. Selmer custom tags/filters can be registered from user code before compiling.
- **No hook exists for**: adding new *kinds* of output pages (search index, category trees) — you'd do that with plain Clojure code in your own `-main` after/around `compile-assets`, which works fine since everything is data.

## 5. Babashka compatibility: **No — Cryogen cannot run under bb**

Blocking, verified from dependency trees and source:
- `cryogen-flexmark` → `com.vladsch.flexmark` (pure-Java markdown parser). bb cannot load arbitrary Java bytecode; flexmark is not built into the bb binary.
- `cryogen-asciidoc` → `asciidoctorj` 2.5.3 (JRuby). Hard no.
- `cryogen-core` itself requires **enlive** (`net.cgrand.enlive-html`, backed by the TagSoup Java parser) and the *entire pipeline* is enlive-DOM-centric (`:content-dom` — TOC, Klipse, descriptions, preview splitting, link rewriting all manipulate enlive nodes). Not bb-compatible and not separable without a rewrite.
- Also JVM-only: `pantomime` (Apache Tika, metadata inference), `net.mikera/imagez` (imaging), `java.text.SimpleDateFormat` usage is fine but flexmark/enlive alone are fatal.
- What *does* carry over to bb: **Selmer is built into babashka**, as are hiccup, cheshire, and `clojure.data.xml`; Sass is an external binary shell-out. So Cryogen's templating/config/output conventions port to bb; its parsing/DOM layer does not. No bb port of Cryogen exists; the bb-native reference point in the ecosystem is borkdude's much simpler `quickblog`.
- Practical consequence: every build is a JVM start (`clojure -M:build` / `lein run`), multi-second startup; watch mode amortizes this in dev but a bb CLI cannot wrap Cryogen in-process — only as a subprocess.

## 6. Maintenance status (August 2026)

**Alive and actively maintained.** Verified from git log and Clojars:
- `cryogen-core` **0.5.1 released June 1, 2026** (Clojars; 87 versions total). Commits May 31–Jun 1 2026: replaced `hawk` watcher with java.nio WatchService, TOC fix, RSS `Date`→`Instant` fix, dependency pinning (bouncycastle, commons-io), Clojure bumped to **1.12.5**.
- `cryogen` lein-template **0.7.9 released June 1, 2026** (113 versions); prior activity Feb 2026.
- Plugins are stable/dormant: cryogen-flexmark last commit June 2021 (flexmark 0.60.2), cryogen-asciidoc similar vintage — they're small and "done", but the pinned flexmark is ~2020-era.
- Community size: cryogen ~1.1k stars, cryogen-core 72 stars; original author Carmen La, active maintainers include Jakub Holý. Docs site cryogenweb.org is current with the code.

## 7. Honest assessment: bending Cryogen into a vdoing-like knowledge base

What vdoing provides that Cryogen lacks structurally:

1. **Nested hierarchical sidebar from numbered directories** (vdoing's core: `docs/01.guide/01.intro.md` → auto-generated collapsible tree, order from numeric prefixes, prefixes stripped from titles/URLs). Cryogen's nav model is **flat**: `group-pages` yields two one-level lists (`navbar-pages`, `sidebar-pages`) from a `:navbar?` flag + `:page-index` int. There is no directory→tree mapping and no tree data structure anywhere. You could build one *without forking core*: `:update-article-fn` to parse numeric prefixes from `:file-name` (derive order, clean `:uri` — `:uri` is just a map key and rewrites propagate to prev/next/sitemap), plus `:extend-params-fn` to fold `site-data`'s `:pages` into a tree. But **Selmer cannot recursively render an arbitrary-depth tree** (no recursive includes/macros), so the sidebar HTML itself would have to be generated in Clojure (hiccup) and injected `|safe`. Entirely feasible — but at that point you have written vdoing's central feature yourself; Cryogen contributed nothing to it.
2. **Card-style home page** (banner, feature cards, recent-posts list): easy. `:home? true` page + custom `home.html`; extra config keys flow through the open config schema to the template. Low effort.
3. **Docs/blog duality**: maps tolerably — posts = blog stream (tags, archives, RSS all free), pages = knowledge base. But tags/categories are **posts-only** in Cryogen; vdoing indexes knowledge-base articles by tag/category too, so you'd reimplement tag aggregation across pages via `extend-params-fn`.
4. **Full-text client-side search**: absent from Cryogen; you'd generate a JSON index (trivial with the hooks, since parsed articles are data) + front-end JS. Standard but additional work.
5. **Theme**: no existing Cryogen theme is remotely vdoing-like; all are blogs. A complete new Selmer theme (layout, collapsible sidebar CSS/JS, right-hand floating TOC, dark mode) is a from-scratch job — though Cryogen's TOC data and prev/next maps feed it nicely.
6. **Front matter**: Cryogen is EDN-only front matter; vdoing content in the wild is YAML front matter — a migration/conversion step (or a custom Markup impl that accepts YAML).

**Verdict**: Cryogen is a well-built, actively maintained *blog* engine whose three hooks (`update-article-fn`, `extend-params-fn`, `postprocess-article-html-fn`) plus open schemas genuinely allow a vdoing-shaped site without forking — estimate: the numbered-dir module, tree builder + hiccup sidebar, new theme, and search index are each modest, and you'd keep tags/RSS/sitemap/archives/watcher for free. But you would be writing ~all of vdoing's distinguishing features on top of it. The **disqualifier for clogem-press is babashka**: Cryogen is irreducibly JVM (flexmark, enlive DOM core, asciidoctorj) and a bb CLI could only shell out to a JVM build. The highest-value takeaways for clogem-press are architectural, not code: the `Markup` protocol (3 methods, reader→HTML string), classpath `plugin.edn` registration, EDN config with `deep-merge` of site + theme config + runtime overrides validated by a schema, EDN-map front matter read off a PushbackReader, the article-as-open-map + three-hook pipeline design, `:clean-urls` tri-mode handling, `:selmer/context` prefix-aware `{% style %}`/`{% script %}` tags, theme-as-directory with its own `config.edn`, and incremental recompilation via a changeset filter. All of these concepts are directly reimplementable on bb (Selmer/hiccup are built in) once flexmark/enlive are replaced with bb-compatible parsing (e.g. markdown via a bb-compatible lib or pod, and hiccup/plain-string HTML assembly instead of an enlive DOM).

Note for GitHub Pages/docs-folder deployment: `:public-dest` is configurable (e.g. "docs") but validated against overlapping `content`/`themes`/`src`/`target`; publishing into a *separate* repo's `docs/` folder is a copy/push step outside Cryogen, and cryogenweb.org has a GitHub Pages guide.
